tags.name: Timber
tags.description: Models where sawn or worked wood dominates the look — the inside of the wood: planks, beams, barrels, crates, furniture, scaffolding and the wooden parts of buildings. The outside of a trunk or branch falls under bark; models with both a cut face and bark carry both tags.

tags.name: Bark
tags.description: Models where the outside of a trunk or branch dominates the look — bark: trees, branches, roots, stumps and rough trunks. Sawn or worked wood falls under timber; trunks and stumps with a cut face carry both tags.

tags.name: Metal
tags.description: Models where metal dominates the look or is the working part: tools and weapons, anvils and grindstones, locks, keys and levers, bars, grates and fittings, lanterns and torches, and the iron and copper from the resources kit. Gold and silver are listed separately under precious-metal. A barrel or chest counts for its hoops and fittings, and so carries both timber and metal.

tags.name: Paper
tags.description: Paper and parchment: books, scrolls, maps and the journal, open and closed.

tags.name: Stone
tags.description: Worked stone: walls, floors, tiles, columns, stairs, quay walls, paving and stepping stones — stone that someone has laid or hewn. The raw rocks and boulders are under rock.

tags.name: Rock
tags.description: Raw stone as it lies in the landscape: boulders, pebbles, gravel, rubble, rock formations and the mountains. Hewn and laid stone is under stone.

tags.name: Soil
tags.description: Loose ground: sand and dirt — the sand and dirt patches of the mini-forest and pirate kits, and the dirt tiles and well base of the village kit. Laid paving and hewn stone are under stone, loose boulders, gravel and rubble under rock. A grass patch is flora sitting on the ground, not soil.

tags.name: Textile
tags.description: Cloth and rope work: tent canvas and canopies, sails and banners, bedding, cloth sacks, the textile stack from the resources kit, the balloon with its baskets, and the wrapped handles of tools and torches. Hide — belts, straps, boots, bags and book covers — is under leather.

tags.name: Leather
tags.description: Tanned hide: belts, straps, boots and shoes, bracers and jerkins, quivers, satchels and backpacks, book covers, and the straps holding a stack of bricks together. A figure in leather carries this tag next to the textile of their cloth.

tags.name: Flora
tags.description: What grows or has grown: trees, stumps, branches, roots and tree trunks, flowers, grass, cattail, mushrooms, cacti, grain and the weeds coming through floors and walls. The living, leafy part additionally carries foliage.

tags.name: Foliage
tags.description: The greenery itself: leafy trees, conifers, palms, grass clumps and grass patches, plants, lily pads and grain. Bare branches, stumps, trunks and dead trees carry only flora.

tags.name: Ceramic
tags.description: Pottery and fired clay: jugs, pitchers, vases, plates, bowls, pots and bottles, and the roof tiles of the fantasy-town and village kits.

tags.name: Bone
tags.description: Bone: the loose bones, ribcage and skull of the halloween kit, and the bone in the meat — the hams of the restaurant kit and the set plates of the dungeon kit.

tags.name: Food
tags.description: Edible matter: bread, cheese, fish and meat, the roast and the stew, and the set plates of the dungeon kit. The bone in the meat carries bone alongside it, and the plate or bowl it is served on carries its own material.

tags.name: Wax
tags.description: Candle wax: the candles from dungeon, props and halloween — loose, thin, melted, triple, lit and snuffed — plus the wall shelf with candles and the decorated floor tile one stands on. Named for the material rather than the object, the way timber and cork are: the candle as a thing carries the fire tag.

tags.name: Glass
tags.description: Glass: bottles and potions, the windows of the village kit and the sailing ships with their windows, and the glass in lanterns, street lamps, compass and magnifying glass.

tags.name: Liquid
tags.description: What a vessel holds rather than what it is made of: the potion in a filled flask. Rule M31 lets it take any band — the colour is the liquid's own and says what it is — while the flask around it follows its glass or ceramic and its stopper the cork.

tags.name: Light
tags.description: Burns and gives light: the lit candles and torch of the dungeon kit, the lanterns of halloween, Taaleiland's lighthouse and the burner flame under the hot-air balloons. Snuffed candles, lamps and torches don't carry it.

tags.name: Rope
tags.description: Rope and cord: the rope bundles from the rpgtools kit, the rigging in masts, rope fences and the rope railings of the village kit, the well and the bell pull, the handles of sack and bucket, the wrapped torch handles and the balloon's lines, and the cords the three pendant necklaces hang from.

tags.name: Cork
tags.description: The stopper in a bottle or potion flask, and anything else cut from cork bark. Rule M25 gives it one colour: taupe 14,3, the same on every model. The bottle or flask it sits in follows its own material, glass or ceramic.

tags.name: Fauna
tags.description: Animal, apart from bone: the shells and starfish from the beach, the two fish from the survival kit, and the sea life from Quaternius — dolphin, whale, shark, manta ray and the loose fish.

tags.name: Precious Metal
tags.description: Gold and silver: the bars, nuggets and stacks from the resources kit, the coins from the dungeon and prototype kits, the gold key and the gold-trimmed chests, and the gold fittings on a keyring, a lock and a compass. Copper and iron are under metal.

tags.name: Gemstone
tags.description: The stone set in a ring, a necklace, an amulet or a hilt. Rule M36 gives it three colours — dark red 8,0, dark green 1,1 or blue 4,2 — and rule M41 asks for this tag, so that a dark red or blue band on a piece of jewellery has a material answering for it instead of passing as an accent. The metal around the stone is precious metal, rule M11, and the cord a pendant hangs from is rope.

tags.name: Special
tags.description: A deliberate exception the PO has approved: the colour and material rules of appendix A do not apply to it. Only the PO assigns this tag — it is not a way to silence a finding you would rather not fix, and every model carrying it should be one you can name the reason for. The whole characters group carries it: the humanoids wear skin tones, dyed cloth and heraldic colours that the prop rules of appendix A do not describe, and the tentacle is grouped with them. The stucco block and half-arch of the village kit carry it for their render, which appendix A gives no material and no band. The heart and star of the platformer kit carry it because they are game pickups: signs, not objects made of anything.

tags.name: Container
tags.description: Anything you can put something in, whatever its size: the bags and the backpack, the barrels, kegs, crates, boxes and buckets, the chests and the small cage, the wooden pallet and the parts pile, and every vessel that holds a liquid — the bottles with their colour variants, the jugs, the filled and empty potions and the two vases. Cuts across the groups on purpose: chests & barrels, bottles & jugs and the resources each deliver part of it, and what goes inside is tagged separately.

tags.name: Gold
tags.description: Reads as gold: the bars, ingots and their stacks, the coins and coin stacks, the gold bag and the gold chest, the four rings, the gold key and rpg-quaternius' key-2, the hanging keyring, the platformer kit's lock and star, the compass base and the coloured two-handed sword. Gold first and silver as the alternative, per appendix A — this tag says what a model looks like, the precious-metal material says what it is made of.

tags.name: Meat
tags.description: Meat and the dishes made of it: the chicken leg and the steak from the food kit, the ham, the steak ingredient and the stew from the restaurant kit, the roast from props, and the dungeon kit's two full plates. The bread, the cheese and the fish are food but not meat and stay out.

tags.name: Key
tags.description: The keys themselves: the dungeon kit's key, the four from rpg-quaternius and the gold and plain metal ones from fantasy-props, plus the keyring and the hanging keyring they hang on. The locks and padlocks they open sit beside them in keys & locks but are not keys.

tags.name: Tableware
tags.description: What goes on the table to eat and drink from: the two bowls, the plates from every kit in both sizes with the plate stack and the fantasy-props table plate, the cups and mugs, and the cutlery — spoon, fork and the three knives. Spread over plates & bowls and cooking & tableware; the pans, pots and campfires you cook on don't reach the table and stay out.

tags.name: Palms
tags.description: Palm trees for beach and island: the three beach palms from the modular-terrain kit, the six from natuur and the three from the Quaternius pirate kit. Split out of the trees group, which also holds the leafy trees and the conifers.

tags.name: Conifers
tags.description: Pines, firs and the other needle trees: the two hilly pines from the modular-terrain kit, the pines from natuur and quaternius-nature, the two orange halloween pines, the four cone-shaped trees from fantasy-town-kit, the two from mini-forest and the two from the survival kit. Their leafless, dead counterparts carry the branch tag instead.

tags.name: Fungi
tags.description: Mushrooms and what they grow on: the four mushrooms from natuur and the overgrown log from quaternius-nature.

tags.name: Cacti
tags.description: Desert plants: the four cacti from quaternius-nature and the four flowering ones beside them.

tags.name: Branch
tags.description: Bare wood without leaves: the loose branches from natuur and the modular-terrain kit, the six roots from natuur, and every leafless tree — the bare trees from natuur and forest, the dead birch, common and willow trees from quaternius-nature, and the three dead trees from halloween. What they're made of is bark and timber; this tag says what the shape is.

tags.name: Ladder
tags.description: What you climb straight up: the ladders from mini-forest, modular-cave-kit, platformer-kit and village-kit, the broken and the long one, and the step ladder from props. The steps you walk up carry the stairs tag.

tags.name: Stairs
tags.description: Steps you walk up: the stone, wooden and walled stairs from the dungeon kit, the wood and stone stairs from fantasy-town-kit with and without handrail, the modular stairs from dungeon-quaternius, and the village kit's wooden steps. What you climb straight up carries the ladder tag.

tags.name: Fences
tags.description: What marks off a path or an area: the fences from fantasy-town-kit, survival-kit and platformer-kit with their corners, curves, gates and rope variants, the board fences, curves and gates from the modular-terrain kit, the platformer kit's poles, the pirate kit's fence structures, the village kit's rope and railing pieces, and the two open castle towers whose sides are railings.

tags.name: Doors
tags.description: Doorways and what closes them: the arch and the arched door from dungeon-quaternius, the stone and stucco doorways from the village kit, the dungeon kit's doorway walls, the wooden door and the doorway walls from fantasy-town-kit, and the gate in the fantasy-town fence.

tags.name: Floor
tags.description: What you stand on once it has been laid down: the wooden and tiled floors from the dungeon kit with their broken, grated and spiked variants and its dirt floors, the village kit's wooden floors, dirt patches and cobblestone transitions, the survival kit's floors, the pirate kit's platforms and docks, the fantasy-town planks, the modular floor layers from dungeon-quaternius and modular-cave-kit, the halloween dirt floor and the beach dock. The bare ground underneath belongs to ground & terrain.

tags.name: Scroll
tags.description: Rolled and loose sheets: the empty and the rolled map from rpgtools, the parchment and the scroll from rpg-quaternius, and the two scrolls from fantasy-props. Paper throughout; the books they sit with live in books & scrolls.

tags.name: Jewellery
tags.description: What you wear: the three pendant necklaces and the four rings from rpg-quaternius. The coins they're worth are tagged separately.

tags.name: Coins
tags.description: Money: the loose coin and the three coin stacks from the dungeon kit, the coin, skull coin and star coin from rpg-quaternius, the pirate kit's heap of coins, and the gold bag and gold chest it's kept in.

tags.name: Furniture
tags.description: What furnishes a room: the beds, the chair, the stool, the tables whole and broken, the shelves and wall shelves from the dungeon kit, the halloween bench and the carpet from props.

tags.name: Roofs
tags.description: What goes on top of a building: the concave, convex and straight roof pieces from the village kit with their corners, eaves and edges, the roof pieces from fantasy-town-kit with the gable parts and the roof window, the village kit's upper window and the roofed well.

tags.name: Barrel
tags.description: Staved and hooped: the barrels from the pirate kit, props, the village kit and the dungeon kit, the village kit's open one and its second shape, and the dungeon kit's keg. Narrower than the container tag, which also covers the crates, boxes, bags and bottles.

tags.name: Bag
tags.description: What you carry over a shoulder: the bags from rpg-quaternius and fantasy-props, the backpack, and the pirates' gold bag. Cloth and leather rather than staves or boards.

tags.name: Chest
tags.description: The lidded chests: the ones from the Quaternius pirate kit, the Kenney pirate kit and the dungeon kit, and the pirates' gold chest. Three of the four open and close on their own animation.

tags.name: Seating
tags.description: What you sit on: the halloween bench, and the chair and the stool from the dungeon kit.

tags.name: Tables
tags.description: What you put things on: the small, medium and long tables from the dungeon kit, with the broken medium and long ones beside them. What goes on top of them carries the tableware tag.

tags.name: Lamp
tags.description: Light in a housing, made to stay where it's put: the street lamp and the wall lamp from the village kit, the rpgtools lantern, the hanging, standing and post lanterns from halloween, and Taaleiland's lighthouse. The open flames beside them carry the fire tag.

tags.name: Fire
tags.description: An open flame or what carries one: the candles from the dungeon kit lit and unlit, thin, melted and triple, the wall shelf with candles on it, the torches from the dungeon kit and rpgtools burnt, lit and mounted, the campfires from natuur, the survival kit and the modular-terrain kit, the loose fire from props, and the lighthouse, whose light is a fire. The lamps that hold their flame in a housing carry the lamp tag as well.

tags.name: Pans
tags.description: What you cook in, over the fire rather than on the table: the cooking pots and the frying pan from the food kit, and the three pots and three pans from the restaurant kit. The plates, bowls and cutlery you then eat from carry the tableware tag.

tags.name: Boats
tags.description: Small craft, rowed or single-sailed: the rowing boats from the pirate kit, the four village-kit boats with and without oars, the boat and the sailing boat from ships-quaternius, the small Quaternius pirate ship, and the paddle you move them with.

tags.name: Ships
tags.description: The big hulls: the plain, pirate and ghost ships from the Kenney pirate kit in every size with the wreck, the large Quaternius pirate ship, the ships-quaternius sailing ship, and the anchor that belongs with them.

tags.name: Window
tags.description: An opening in a wall you look through: the twelve stucco windows from the village kit in their single, double and rounded forms, narrow and wide, plain and tall, with its upper straight window, and the dungeon kit's window walls — open and closed, scaffolded, and the arched ones gated and open. The gap in the dungeon kit's broken wall counts as one too. The doorways you walk through carry the doors tag.

tags.name: Skull
tags.description: A skull, loose or worn: the loose skulls from dungeon-quaternius, rpg-quaternius, halloween and the Quaternius pirate kit with its pile of them, the four KayKit skeletons and the Quaternius one, the skull on the KayKit skeleton staff and large shield, and the skull flag on the three pirate ships. The headless pirate skeleton is the one skeleton without one, so it stays out.

tags.name: Nature
tags.description: What is already there without anyone doing anything: ground, trees, plants, seabed and rocks. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Structure
tags.description: What has been built: building kits, structures, stairs and bridges, fences. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Object
tags.description: Loose things you place or pick up: furniture, ships, food, chests, resources, tools, signs, items and lights. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Kenney
tags.description: Kits from Kenney (kenney.nl). One hand, one scale: everything comes from the same tile and the props fit together. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: KayKit
tags.description: Kits from Kay Lousberg (kaylousberg.com): dungeon, forest, halloween, resources, restaurant and rpgtools, plus the two character packs — adventurers and skeletons — with the weapons and shields they carry. Consistent style and level of detail across the set. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Quaternius
tags.description: Kits from Quaternius (quaternius.com): fantasy-props and quaternius-nature, plus the six packs that came later — pirate, dungeon, RPG, food, fish and ships. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Animation
tags.description: Carries its own animations in the .glb — chests and doors that open and close, a lever that flips, a compass that opens. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Modular
tags.description: Clicks onto the grid with matching pieces: the walls, roofs, pillars and floors of the three building kits. You don't place them loose but build something out of them, and they only fit within their own kit. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.

tags.name: Assembly
tags.description: Not one thing but a little scene that's finished as it stands: a set table, a stack of crates, a chest full of bottles, the bars and stacks from the resources kit. Derived from the models themselves, so not tracked in catalog/tags.json.
